item.text: I have enough material to synthesize. I’m not searching further; I’m assembling the strongest direct positives and negatives into claim-level items and noting where evidence is still thin.

**Bottom Line**
Tshisekedi’s 2024 record is mostly negative on 5B.5. There is some evidence of anti-corruption signaling and oversight support, but the strongest evidence still points to opaque public finance, weak accountability, and resource-use patterns that looked vulnerable to capture rather than resistant to it.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Le chef de l'Etat a assisté à l'ouverture de la session extraordinaire du Conseil supérieur de la Cour des comptes](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes) | Présidence RDC | 2024-10-07 | Tshisekedi publicly backed the Court of Accounts’ control function, and the court said his support helped revive anti-corruption oversight and public-finance control. This is the clearest pro-evidence for resisting corruption and favoritism, though it is executive-hosted rather than proof of fully independent oversight. | `5B.5` `5B.4` `E0274`

- [Deux nouveaux programmes avec le FMI: Aimé Boji et Doudou Fwamba étaient devant la presse](https://budget.gouv.cd/deux-nouveaux-programmes-avec-le-fmi-aime-boji-et-doudou-fwamba-etaient-devant-la-presse/) | Ministère du Budget | 2024-11-15 | The budget ministry said the finance and budget ministers jointly presented the new IMF programs and credited improved coordination since June 2024. That suggests the economic team was being used to execute reforms, not simply bypassed by patronage networks. | `5B.5` `5B.4` `5B.2` `E0341`

- [IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with the Democratic Republic of Congo on an Extended Credit Facility and a Resilience and Sustainability Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/11/13/pr-24416-drc-imf-reaches-agreement-on-ecf-and-rsf) | IMF | 2024-11-13 | The IMF program explicitly called for better governance, transparency, tighter spending-chain controls, lower tax exemptions, better customs enforcement, and insulation from volatile extractive revenues. This is positive evidence that the administration at least adopted an anti-capture reform agenda. | `5B.5` `5B.4` `5B.3` `E0338`

- [Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts: report](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/) | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. This is direct negative evidence for corruption resistance and public-finance integrity. | `5B.5` `5B.4` `5B.3` `E0353`

- [DRC president Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty said public resources were being squandered, social services were underfunded, and mining expansion was driving forced evictions and pollution. That is strong negative evidence for capture-resistant governance, especially in extractives and state spending. | `5B.5` `5B.4` `E0354`

- [Human Rights Agenda: Democratic Republic of Congo](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/human-rights-agenda-democratic-republic-congo) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-06 | HRW said the government had made little progress on systemic reforms and called for anti-corruption safeguards and stronger institutions. This is indirect but useful evidence that institutional resistance to favoritism and abuse was still weak in practice. | `5B.5` `5B.4` `E0268`

- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Congo, Democratic Republic of: April 2024 - Datasheet](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099434404082425237) | World Bank | 2024-04-03 | The World Bank said growth prospects were favorable, but living standards would not improve without much more ambitious reforms and that deficits, inflation, and downside risks remained. This is indirect counterevidence: the broader rule environment still did not look capture-resistant or reliably pro-competition. | `5B.5` `5B.4` `E0328`

- [The government framed P-DDRCS as a stabilization, peace, and cohesion program](https://acp.cd/nation/programme-de-desarmement-et-demobilisation-une-alternative-pour-la-paix-et-la-cohesion-sociale/) | ACP | 2024-03-22 | The government described P-DDRCS as a stabilization program meant to restore state authority where absent. This is only weak positive evidence, but it points to state-building rather than open patronage of armed or political clients. | `5B.5` `5B.3` `E0346`

**Search Gap**
I found clear evidence of weak anti-corruption performance and public-finance opacity, plus some real oversight and IMF-backed reform signaling. I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Tshisekedi directly dismantled oligarchic networks, broke monopolies, or stripped politically connected businesses of special privileges. The positive side is mostly reform language and oversight support; the negative side is actual governance outcomes and opaque spending.
